topic: Weak-separation honest-inference frontier for exact close-comparison panels. With finitely many treated stacks and candidate donors, iid within-group micro-panels, and a joint asymptotically linear pre-equality-score/post-mean vector, define the nonempty close set by exact zero score and require every close donor to imply the same ATT. Construct simultaneous joint donor-label/ATT Gaussian inversion with within-label outcome uncertainty. Prove uniform coverage, oracle root-n diameter under fixed separation, and a matching positive local-minimax expected-diameter frontier over root-n-separated triangular arrays, including multiple-close-donor faces and shared-control covariance. Reanalyse the CMS State Innovation Models comparison-state claims workflow. PRESOLVE EVIDENCE REQUIRING VERIFICATION: Profiling each joint Wald ellipsoid yields an explicit labelwise interval centered at the post-effect estimate corrected by its score regression; a Gaussian maximum critical value makes the hull cover every true label simultaneously. On the unscaled weak-risk scale, post-mean noise vanishes and the problem reduces to a finite Gaussian label-confidence experiment on a union of coordinate hyperplanes. For two donors with identity score covariance, switches h=(0,c) and h=(c,0), effect gap Delta, and total-variation distance 2 Phi(c/sqrt(2))-1 force honest expected diameter at least Delta times [1-2 alpha-TV]_+; c=1, Delta=0.4, alpha=0.05 gives about 0.1518. Fixed separation eliminates false labels and restores the oracle root-n hull. UNRESOLVED BOTTLENECK: Prove uniform Le Cam minimax equivalence for the nonclosed triangular union and show that covariance-estimated simultaneous inversion attains the finite-Gaussian worst expected-diameter functional, including multiple-zero-label faces. EARLY KILL TEST: Solve the two-donor identity-covariance Gaussian decision problem over 0<c<=H analytically or by a fine-grid linear program and compare its exact minimax diameter with the proposed maximum-critical hull; a persistent sharpness gap not repairable within joint inversion should pivot or stop the run.

open_problems.open_problem: Characterize the minimax worst-case expected diameter of honest ATT confidence sets in the finite Gaussian experiment where at least one donor score is exactly zero and all zero-score donors share one ATT, and determine whether maximum-critical labelwise hull inversion is optimal on two-donor and multiple-zero faces.

source_refs.claim: Inference after noisy option selection requires correction; projection intervals are universally valid but can be substantially less precise than selection-tailored procedures.
source_refs.author: Isaiah Andrews, Toru Kitagawa, and Adam McCloskey

source_refs.claim: Bayes-minimax duality characterizes confidence sets minimizing worst-case expected measure for restricted Gaussian location parameters.
source_refs.author: Steven N. Evans, Ben B. Hansen, and Philip B. Stark

source_refs.claim: Universal post-selection validity follows from simultaneous inference, but the simultaneity insurance can be conservative for a particular selection rule.
source_refs.author: Richard Berk, Lawrence Brown, Andreas Buja, Kai Zhang, and Linda Zhao

source_refs.excerpt: Uniform validity does not determine admissibility or minimax width at a discontinuous collision.
The matching union-honest upper interval and exact expected-length frontier remain open
Replace the Bonferroni half-width by a simultaneous critical-value construction with a proved bounded critical value

open_problems.why_unsolved: The prior collision and near-tie projects establish the same union-honesty obstruction but explicitly leave admissibility, minimax width, and the matching upper procedure unresolved. Existing post-selection theory treats argmax winners or generic model selection, while restricted-Gaussian minimax theory treats ordinary parameter spaces. Exact donor validity instead yields a stratified union indexed by zero score coordinates, and the ATT coordinates are constrained to agree only on the active face. At multiple-zero faces both the selected label set and target map are discontinuous, so simultaneous coverage alone does not identify the least-favorable prior, the optimal adaptation penalty, or whether taking the hull of labelwise intervals is decision-theoretically optimal.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: An exact formula or finite-dimensional primal-dual program for the Gaussian minimax expected-diameter functional, an attaining confidence-set rule or quantitative counterexample to maximum-critical inversion, and a corollary giving oracle root-n diameter under fixed donor separation.

writing_exemplar.why: Its motivation moves from a consequential choice based on noisy estimates to the coverage and interval-length cost of valid post-selection inference.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Noisy estimates determine which comparison is retained -> conventional inference ignores that data-dependent choice -> projection is honest but can be wide -> characterize the shortest honest interval for exact-donor selection

method_exemplars.technique: Convert coverage-constrained confidence rules by Bayes-minimax duality into an optimization over acceptance regions, producing lower bounds and attaining sets.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The requested object is also a minimax expected-measure confidence set in a Gaussian experiment, but on a union of donor-label faces rather than an interval.

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt two-point expected-length lower bounds and ordered between-class moduli to pairs of Gaussian label faces carrying separated ATT values.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The frontier asks for the exact cost of honesty over a union while retaining shorter intervals on the fixed-separated oracle submodel.

method_exemplars.technique: Obtain post-selection validity by simultaneously covering every candidate linear target before the selection rule is applied.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The proposed maximum-critical hull is a structured form of this simultaneity insurance, so its conservatism is the relevant benchmark.

open_problems.open_problem: Prove uniform Le Cam equivalence between fixed-label iid micro-panel experiments and the covariance-indexed finite Gaussian donor-label experiment over root-n-separated triangular arrays, including multiple-zero-label faces and consistently estimated shared-control covariance.

source_refs.claim: Uniform GMM inference is established over drifting sequences spanning unidentified, weakly identified, semi-strong, and strongly identified regimes.
source_refs.author: Donald W. K. Andrews and Xu Cheng

source_refs.claim: Moment-condition inference without identification-strength assumptions is reduced to a Gaussian problem with a functional nuisance parameter, enabling uniformly size-correct conditional tests.
source_refs.author: Isaiah Andrews and Anna Mikusheva

source_refs.claim: Gaussian and multiplier-bootstrap approximations for maxima allow unknown covariance and arbitrary coordinate correlation under stated moment conditions.
source_refs.author: Victor Chernozhukov, Denis Chetverikov, and Kengo Kato

open_problems.why_unsolved: A joint asymptotically linear score/post-mean vector does not by itself transfer expected-diameter risk through the discontinuous rule that decides which score coordinates are exactly zero. Drifting-sequence GMM theory handles changing identification strength, and Gaussian conditional-inference theory removes identification assumptions in smooth moment models, but neither proves deficiency convergence for a causal target defined on a nonclosed finite union of label faces. Gaussian-max approximation permits estimated arbitrary covariance but does not establish experiment-level equivalence or transfer of an unbounded diameter loss. The first missing step is a uniform LAN or Markov-kernel approximation on the stratified triangular class, followed by uniform integrability or truncation sufficient for minimax-risk transfer.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A uniform deficiency-distance theorem for the micro-panel experiment and finite Gaussian label experiment, plus a risk-transfer corollary showing that Gaussian coverage and minimax expected-diameter bounds remain valid for feasible covariance-estimated procedures.

writing_exemplar.why: It uses failure of regular approximations under weak identification to make a Gaussian limit experiment the organizing object for uniform inference.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Standard asymptotics rely on stable identification -> local weak regimes change the limiting experiment -> Gaussian conditional inference restores uniform size -> establish the corresponding experiment for weakly separated donor labels

method_exemplars.technique: Index asymptotics by drifting identification sequences and use subsequence arguments to prove confidence-set validity uniformly across all strength regimes.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Root-n donor-score separations are the analogue of drifting identification strength, with fixed separation as the strong-identification endpoint.

method_exemplars.technique: Extract a sufficient statistic for the Gaussian nuisance function and invert conditional tests with size uniform in identification strength.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The donor-score mean is a finite-dimensional nuisance governing the active face, while the common ATT is the parameter of interest.

method_exemplars.technique: Combine Gaussian comparison, anti-concentration, and multiplier bootstrap arguments to replace an unknown covariance matrix in a maximum statistic.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Simultaneous donor-label inversion uses a Gaussian maximum with correlations induced by shared treated stacks and reused controls.

open_problems.open_problem: For exact close-comparison panels with finitely many labels and diverging unequal within-label micro samples, derive a feasible joint donor-label/ATT Gaussian inversion that propagates post-outcome uncertainty and remains uniformly valid when controls are reused across stacks and several labels have zero scores.

source_refs.claim: Inference with finitely many policy-changing groups is obtained by using an asymptotically large sample of nonchanging groups.
source_refs.author: Timothy G. Conley and Christopher R. Taber

source_refs.claim: Few-treated-group DiD inference is made robust to group-size heteroskedasticity, but the reference distribution still comes from many controls.
source_refs.author: Bruno Ferman and Cristine Pinto

open_problems.why_unsolved: The CMS workflow retains only two or three comparison states but has many beneficiaries within each state, whereas canonical few-policy-change methods obtain their reference distribution from many untreated groups and synthetic-control inference obtains replication over time. None propagates uncertainty about which fixed comparison labels satisfy an exact pre-equality restriction. The prior panel-band construction retains shared primitive-cell covariance for fixed event-horizon labels, not labels whose validity is inferred jointly with their ATT. Here score regression changes each labelwise ATT influence function, unequal micro-sample rates change scaling, reused comparison states correlate labels, and multiple-zero faces make the projection nonsmooth; marginal intervals or diagonal covariance therefore omit both within-label outcome noise and cross-label dependence.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A stacked asymptotically linear score/ATT representation, an explicit uniformly consistent shared-control covariance estimator, and an implementable max-Gaussian or multiplier inversion with uniform ATT coverage and oracle root-n hull diameter under fixed separation.

writing_exemplar.why: It supplies the destination workflow: finitely many selected comparison states, payer-specific claims availability, annual weighting, and reported DiD effects.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: CMS needs comparison states for statewide claims evaluation -> baseline distance ranks a small donor set -> donor availability and weighting vary by payer and year -> inference should propagate donor-label and shared-control uncertainty into the ATT

method_exemplars.technique: Model heteroskedastic group-level pre-post errors induced by unequal micro sample sizes and calibrate inference using an estimable variance relation.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The destination also has fixed policy groups and unequal group sizes, but must replace the many-control reference distribution by within-group influence-function Gaussianity.

method_exemplars.technique: Estimate the law of a correlated maximum using conditional Gaussian multipliers and control covariance replacement by anti-concentration.
method_exemplars.why_closest: One critical value must cover all candidate labels despite dependence from common treated stacks and reused controls.

method_exemplars.technique: Cross-fit the synthetic-control bias correction and prove a self-normalized pivotal limit law for an average causal effect.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It is a concrete ATT estimator-and-limit-law benchmark; the new proof replaces time-series replication by within-label micro-panel replication and retains label uncertainty.

open_problems.open_problem: Replace exact donor-score equality by prespecified equivalence margins and bounded disagreement among donor-specific counterfactual trends, and derive the sharp ATT interval and uniformly valid post-selection confidence set that nest exact-close-donor inversion when the margins vanish.

source_refs.claim: Equivalence tests can provide evidence that pre-trend differences lie within a prespecified tolerance, unlike failure to reject an exact-equality null.
source_refs.author: Holger Dette and Martin Schumann

source_refs.claim: Synthetic-control estimators are generally biased under imperfect pretreatment fit when assignment correlates with unobserved confounders, so validity requires additional application-specific structure.
source_refs.author: Bruno Ferman and Cristine Pinto

source_refs.claim: Restrictions linking post-treatment violations to observed pre-trend differences partially identify treatment effects and support uniformly valid sensitivity analysis.
source_refs.author: Ashesh Rambachan and Jonathan Roth

source_refs.claim: Conditional, projection, and hybrid confidence intervals can be uniformly valid for interval-identified treatment or policy parameters selected from an estimated set.
source_refs.author: Sukjin Han and Adam McCloskey

source_refs.excerpt: Replace the oracle bridge with either an estimated/identified bridge class or a joint interval over plausible a_s

open_problems.why_unsolved: Equivalence testing decides whether a pre-trend discrepancy is smaller than a chosen margin but does not map every passing donor to a common causal ATT or quantify disagreement across simultaneously plausible donors. Sensitivity analysis bounds trend violations for a specified comparison structure, while imperfect-fit results show that near-zero scores alone do not remove confounding. The banked synthetic-control proposal further conditions its interval on a fixed oracle bridge and asks for a joint interval over plausible bridges. Once labels and bridge maps vary together, the identified set is a nonregular union whose endpoints change when labels enter or leave; selected-set inference presumes those endpoints are already defined and therefore does not establish sharpness here.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A sharp finite-dimensional optimization or support-function formula for the ATT set over all labels and bridge maps satisfying score margins and trend-disagreement bounds, plus uniformly valid endpoint inference with an explicit exact-zero limit.

writing_exemplar.why: Its framing replaces an implausible exact parallel-trends assertion by an interpretable sensitivity class and asks which causal conclusions survive.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Exact parallel trends is not empirically defensible -> pre-period discrepancies calibrate structured violations -> effects become partially identified -> build donor-equivalence sensitivity regions with honest inference

method_exemplars.technique: Encode permitted trend violations as convex restrictions, project them onto the causal contrast, and characterize the resulting identified set.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Score margins and bounded cross-donor disagreement likewise form a finite convex feasibility problem whose projection is the sharp ATT interval.

method_exemplars.technique: Combine least-favorable and conditional critical values for uniformly valid subvector inference while adapting to slack and binding inequalities.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Donors outside the equivalence margin act like slack restrictions, while several boundary donors create the analogue of multiple binding moments.

method_exemplars.technique: Construct conditional, projection, and hybrid intervals for a causal parameter selected from an estimated set and prove uniform asymptotic validity.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The destination also combines data-dependent set membership with an interval-valued ATT, after the donor-validity set and ATT bounds are derived jointly.

literature_map:
CMS/RTI (2018) used a two-stage claims workflow: rank states by baseline Euclidean distance, retain two or three, then apply annual person-level propensity and balancing weights.
The CMS appendix reports unstable Mahalanobis scores with many characteristics and changing Medicaid donors when claims lacked run-out, making donor choice empirical rather than fixed.
Abadie-Diamond-Hainmueller (2010) and Arkhangelsky-Athey-Hirshberg-Imbens-Wager (2021) anchor comparative-case and synthetic-DiD estimation but do not solve exact finite-label ambiguity.
Ferman-Pinto (2021) show that imperfect pretreatment fit can leave synthetic controls biased, so a near-zero score is not automatically causal validity.
Chernozhukov-Wuthrich-Zhu (2021) provide conformal counterfactual inference, while their 2026 JPE paper gives cross-fitted self-normalized ATT inference under time-series rather than micro-panel asymptotics.
Roth (2022) shows that pre-trend screening can have low power and distort subsequent effect inference, motivating joint donor-screen and ATT inference.
Dette-Schumann (2024) replace failure to reject exact pre-trend equality by equivalence testing; Rambachan-Roth (2023) turn bounded violations into honest partial-identification sensitivity analysis.
Conley-Taber (2011) and Ferman-Pinto (2019) cover finitely many treated groups but rely on many comparisons; CMS has fixed comparison labels and many individuals per label.
Berk-Brown-Buja-Zhang-Zhao (2013) obtain universal post-selection validity by simultaneity, whose conservatism makes expected-diameter optimality live.
Andrews-Kitagawa-McCloskey (2024) develop conditional, projection, and hybrid Gaussian inference after selection; exact-zero set selection has different face geometry.
McCloskey (2024) and Han-McCloskey (2026) preserve uniform validity for selected models or interval-identified parameters but do not derive donor-label identified sets.
Andrews-Cheng (2014) and Andrews-Mikusheva (2016) supply drifting-identification and Gaussian conditional-inference machinery, not Le Cam equivalence for the nonclosed donor union.
Andrews-Roth-Pakes (2023) adapt critical values to slack versus binding inequalities, paralleling far versus close donors and multiple-close faces.
Chernozhukov-Chetverikov-Kato (2013) justify covariance-estimated Gaussian maxima under arbitrary dependence.
Evans-Hansen-Stark (2005) provide the decision-duality template for deciding whether a maximum-critical hull is minimax in expected diameter.
